checks.label: Every equation loses the smaller number of x's from both sides, and the answer makes both sides of the first equation worth the same: 5x + 2 = 3x + 10 leaves 2x + 2 = 10 and x = 4 (22 each); 4x + 1 = 2x + 7 leaves 2x + 1 = 7 and x = 3 (13); 4x + 6 = 2x + 16, x = 5 (26); 4x + 1 = x + 13, x = 4 (17); x + 7 = 3x + 1 leaves 7 = 2x + 1 and x = 3 (10); 2x + 12 = 6x, x = 3 (18); 7x − 5 = 4x + 10, x = 5 (30); 4x − 6 = x + 12, x = 6 (18); 2x + 11 = 4x + 3, x = 4 (19); 3x − 4 = x + 6, x = 5 (11)
A formula remains balanced if we perform the same operation to both sides of it
Equations with unknowns on both sides can be manipulated so that the unknowns are on one side, and then solved
When solving x + 7 = 3x + 1, one +1 tile and one +x tile on both sides can be removed
Start with the last operation and work back to the first

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives, its check failing: the x's off the left side only, or moved across and added; the number with x added to the other side, not taken off; the other side divided but not that number; or 4x = 12 read as x = 12

Every picture, finished, shows its answer: the balance level with the same boxes off both pans or the answer in every box and both sides worth the same; a slip tips it in the warning colour, or its check fails; and each flow diagram lights its two undo steps and ends on the check
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer: every box still reads x, no side's worth or working is written, and the flow diagram's undo is still to fill in

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s; boxes come off a pair at a time at least 0.2 s apart, and other parts (a guess counted when its labels arrive) at least 0.45 s apart, each once the travel before it has ended
